Rule 9 (cite.py --check 8.8.2 'the operation shall proceed as though the shorter operand were extended on the right by a sufficient number of boolean zeros' -> OK 9)) has four halves, all verified: usage-independence, shift result length = first item, positionwise combine, right zero-extension. The refuter's one divergence - a relation whose boolean operand carries only a shift missed the boolean channel - is closed by PB1412, and pb1412_shift_only_boolean_conditions pins the two halves no spec-derived test had: S2 = B"10" B-SHIFT-LC 1 = B"01" true and = B"000001" false (the result is as long as the FIRST item; a shift over a longer extended item answers the opposite on both), and a USAGE BIT item shifts like a PIC 1 item (UB B-SHIFT-R 1 = 0110). The positionwise and extension halves are CobolBoolTests. [editions: the shift half 2023 only (Annex E.2 item 3); the rest 2002+]
